tiers.name: Water trough and a lambing pen
A proper barn with a roof that keeps its tiles
Stud board, loose boxes and a vet on speed dial

events.line: A fox got in the night before and the hens, the ducks and your afternoon all went with it. The fence was mended by teatime.
A visiting breed judge leant on the gate for an hour and said "hm" four times. Three owners booked a stall before she left.
A heat wave. The stock stood under the one tree in a queue, and the water trough was drunk dry twice.
Lambing open day. Half the parish came for the lambs and stayed for the tea urn.
A wet week turned the gateway to soup. The boarders were unbothered and everyone else sulked.
The vet came out for a limp that turned out to be a stone. The bill for the stone was not small.
A hard frost split the trough. The ice came out in one piece and was admired for some time.

upgrades.name: A vet on a retainer
upgrades.text: A fixed fee a month and nobody panics at midnight.

upgrades.name: Stabling for six more
upgrades.text: More horses, more carrots, more muck.

upgrades.name: A little show yard
upgrades.text: Gymkhanas and clinics bring a better class of visitor. And a worse class of weather.

asks.title: The pony club rally
asks.text: The local pony club would like to use {deed} for its summer rally. There will be forty children, thirty ponies and an unspecified number of parents.

options.label: Host it properly, with a tea tent
options.say: Forty children, thirty ponies and a tea tent that runs out of squash at eleven. A great success.

risk.say: It rains, the tea tent floods, and a pony eats the bunting. Memorable for the wrong reasons.

options.label: Let them have the far field and leave them to it
options.say: The children are happy. The field is mostly intact.

options.label: Say you are fully booked
options.say: The rally goes to a farm up the road.
